response.sql:
WITH city_counts AS (
    SELECT z.city, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS member_count
    FROM attendance AS a
    JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member
    JOIN zip_code AS z ON z.zip_code = m.zip
    GROUP BY z.city
),
city_shares AS (
    SELECT city, member_count,
           1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM city_counts
),
scored AS (
    SELECT member_count, share,
           AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share
    FROM city_shares
)
SELECT AVG(member_count) AS average_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM scored
WHERE share > average_share;

assumptions.assumption: Cities are identified by the zip_code.city value, and “all cities” means cities represented by at least one attending member with a matching ZIP record.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every city in zip_code when calculating the overall average share, including cities with no attending members (which have a count and share of zero).
alternatives.sql:
WITH all_cities AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT city FROM zip_code
),
city_counts AS (
    SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS member_count
    FROM all_cities AS c
    LEFT JOIN zip_code AS z ON z.city = c.city
    LEFT JOIN member AS m ON m.zip = z.zip_code
    LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id
    GROUP BY c.city
),
city_shares AS (
    SELECT city, member_count,
           1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM city_counts
),
scored AS (
    SELECT member_count, share,
           AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share
    FROM city_shares
)
SELECT AVG(member_count) AS average_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM scored
WHERE share > average_share;
